record.paper: Burling graphs, chromatic number, and orthogonal tree-decompositions

dossier_meta.paper: Burling graphs, chromatic number, and orthogonal tree-decompositions
dossier_meta.statement_text: There exists a function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that $\chi(G) \leq f(k)$ for every $k \geq 1$ and every graph $G$ admitting a spaghetti tree-decomposition $(T, \{B_t\}_{t \in V(T)})$ and a path-decomposition $(P, \{B_p\}_{p \in V(P)})$ such that $|B_t \cap B_p| \leq k$ for every $t \in V(T)$ and $p \in V(P)$.
dossier_meta.context_text: The authors conclude the paper with this conjecture as an open problem in the spirit of exploring how the Asplund–Grünbaum result could be extended. A spaghetti tree-decomposition is a tree-decomposition rooted at some vertex $r$ such that, orienting edges away from $r$, the subtree induced by bags containing any fixed vertex $v$ forms a directed path. The authors remark that the conjecture could even hold with two spaghetti tree-decompositions.
